bib.title: Follow the Entities: A Corpus Map for Agentic Search

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Follow the Entities: A CorpusMap for Agentic Search", Soyeong Jeong (KAIST, work done at Microsoft), Sujay Kumar Jauhar, Sung Ju Hwang, Andrew Joohun Nam. Preprint, arXiv:2609.37226v1 [cs.CL], 29 Sep 2026.

COVERAGE: All 29 pages read, via extraction of 98,892 chars (the first call reported 98,235, the second 98,892; same file, a counting difference). Main text, Tables 1-10, Figures 1-6 and Appendices A and B were read in full. References were skimmed for origins. Appendix C (pp. 21-29, the prompts in Figures 7-13) was only spot-checked, since it holds prompts and no results. The paper has no separate Limitations section. Figures were seen as extracted text and captions only, not rendered.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. CorpusMap beats raw-corpus agentic search on quality while using fewer input tokens.
 - number: +6.4 to +11.7 Overall Quality points, 34-57% fewer input tokens
 - setup: 4 GPT models (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Luna/Terra/Sol), 3 benchmarks, multi-document questions only, a terminal agent using find/grep/cat, means over 3 runs. The same LLM builds the map and answers.
 - quote: "CORPUSMAP improves overall quality by 6.4 to 11.7 points while using 34% to 57% fewer input tokens on average"
 - where: p.3 (intro). Table 1, p.7. Table 6 gives paired-bootstrap 95% CIs, with raw-corpus gains of +6.45, +11.74, +6.76 and +7.00 (GPT-5.5, Luna, Terra, Sol), all p<1e-4. The bootstrap resamples questions only.
2. Table 1 numbers for GPT-5.5. Overall Quality is 72.55 for CorpusMap against 66.11 for RawCorpus. Relative tokens are 0.43x. Oracle (gold documents only) is 79.62. Luna goes 53.85 to 65.58. Sol goes 67.69 to 74.68.
 - Document recall on EnterpriseRAG-Bench (GPT-5.5): 76.17 vs 61.62.
 - Correctness on EnterpriseRAG-Bench (GPT-5.5): 73.75 vs 62.08.
 - quote: "CORPUSMAP(Ours) 76.17±0.30 73.75±1.77 79.88±1.00 88.1k 82.70±0.79 70.68±0.83 74.5k 64.37±0.89 494.7k 72.55 0.43×"
 - where: Table 1, p.7
3. Other ways of organizing the corpus do not reliably beat the raw corpus. Only the entity map does.
 - number: for example Corpus2Skill scores 45.49 against 66.11 for Raw on GPT-5.5, and GroupPage scores 31.23 on Sol.
 - quote: "the four baselines that organize the corpus in other ways do not consistently improve over RAWCORPUS, indicating that simply adding a navigation layer does not guarantee improvement"
 - where: p.6. The baselines are DocumentPage, GroupPage, LLM Wiki (Karpathy 2026) and Corpus2Skill (Sun et al. 2026a). Table 6 gives CorpusMap's margin over each.
 - setup: Table 1 setup. Document pages on Sol used 3.94x the tokens of Raw.
4. It also beats retrieve-then-generate baselines, including HippoRAG and GraphRAG. This is the claim closest to notes 01 and 11.
 - number: GPT-5.5 Quality 76.60 for CorpusMap vs BM25 63.66, Dense 65.05, HippoRAG 64.66, GraphRAG 47.95, Raw 65.60. Luna: 73.20 vs 60.78, 58.84, 61.74, 43.46, 63.31.
 - setup: EnterpriseRAG-Bench only (80 multi-document questions). The LLM answers from a fixed retrieved context without full corpus access. HippoRAG is within about 1 point of BM25 and dense, and GraphRAG is far below them.
 - quote: "CORPUSMAPoutperforms all of them with both LLMs, including the graph-based HippoRAG and GraphRAG."
 - where: Table 3 and p.7
 - Note the comparison mixes paradigms: agent with map versus a fixed-context retriever.
5. The map is built once and amortised, and a cheap model can build it for stronger ones to use.
 - number: break-even at 9.0K queries (GPT-5.5), 12.4K (Sol), 17.3K (Terra) and 26.3K (Luna). One-time build cost is ≤$4,732.14 (GPT-5.5 builder), ≤$2,681.76 (Sol), ≤$74.65 (Luna) and $310.58 (DeepSeek).
 - Luna-built map: 73.59 with a GPT-5.5 answerer and 74.68 with Sol, against 65.60 and 69.54 for Raw.
 - setup: EnterpriseRAG-Bench. The cost prices are the authors' estimates from August-September 2026 API pricing. Break-even values are read from the Figure 5 labels.
 - quote: "the construction cost of the map is recovered as it is reused across queries."
 - where: Table 4 p.8, Figure 5 p.17
 - Quote for the cross-builder result: "even the map constructed by the least expensive LLM, at a small fraction of the cost of the most expensive one, improves the overall quality over RAWCORPUS for every answering LLM".
6. The map works without LLM calls.
 - number: no table, so it is read off Figure 4 only (a figure, not a number)
 - setup: GLinker (Stepanov et al. 2026, open GLiNER models) does extraction and linking, and pages are rendered with no LLM. Tested with GPT-5.6 Luna and Qwen3.8-27B, with corpora of 2.8k, 10k and 20k documents plus distractors.
 - quote: "the resulting map is comparably effective to the LLM-constructed map, and outperforms RAWCORPUS on every metric at a lower cost"
 - where: p.9, Figure 4
7. The map can be updated incrementally.
 - number: tokens saved over a full rebuild of 34%, 69% and 71% at updates 1, 2 and 3 (read from the Figure 3a axis labels). Correctness on newly covered questions gains +30.4, +40.0 and +40.0 points (Figure 3c).
 - setup: EnterpriseRAG-Bench ordered chronologically, GPT-5.5. The final map matches a full rebuild "comparably", with no figure given.
 - quote: "each incremental update saves a substantial fraction of the construction tokens of a full rebuild"
 - where: p.8, Figure 3
8. Candidate file paths matter, and relevant ones are what help.
 - number: GPT-5.5 Quality and tokens on EnterpriseRAG-Bench:
 - CorpusMap without candidates: 69.04, 496.4k.
 - With relevant candidate linked documents (the default): 76.60, 88.1k.
 - With random candidate linked documents: 60.76, 413.5k.
 - Raw corpus: 65.60, 206.5k.
 - Raw corpus given relevant candidates: 66.19, 107.4k.
 - Mechanism: BM25 over Entity Pages pools the linked documents, which are then reranked by BM25.
 - quote: "CORPUSMAP w/ Candidate Entity-Linked Docs 76.60 88.1k 60.76 413.5k"
 - where: Table 8 p.18, Section B.3. Quality is stable beyond about 1 candidate (Figure 6). The ablation is only on this one benchmark and model.
9. Direct entity-entity edges, as in a knowledge graph, do not help.
 - number: document recall changes only -2.6 to +0.2 points. Entity pages grow 27-52% and input tokens rise by up to 28%. Agents use the edges in 11-19% of questions, 71% of those moves find no new gold document, and 86-90% of newly opened pages are found by search anyway.
 - quote: "document recall changes by only −2.6 to +0.2 points, while these edges enlarge Entity Pages by 27–52% on average and increase input tokens by up to 28%."
 - where: p.19, Section B.4
 - setup: GPT-5.5 on EnterpriseRAG-Bench. This argues against a GraphRAG-style relation graph when bipartite entity-document links exist.
10. The finding holds across other models, and the cheap model gains most on raw search.
 - number: Table 2 (EnterpriseRAG-Bench). DeepSeek-V4-Pro goes 68.02 to 71.11 and MAI-Thinking-1 goes 34.06 to 45.07.
 - Judge robustness: re-judging with DeepSeek-V4-Pro keeps CorpusMap first on all five judged metrics.
 - Kendall's τ is 1.00 on three metrics, 0.83 on WixQA factuality, and 0.47 on WixQA context recall.
 - where: Table 2 p.7, Table 7 p.17
 - On the remaining, mostly single-document EnterpriseRAG-Bench questions, correctness is 94.76 vs 89.05 and tokens 171.7k vs 250.7k (Table 5, p.16).
11. Per-benchmark gains differ a lot. On HERB with GPT-5.5, content is 64.37 vs 62.31, so most of the gain comes from EnterpriseRAG-Bench and WixQA. For Luna on HERB it is 50.45 vs 44.86. Tokens on HERB for GPT-5.5 fall from 598.4k to 494.7k.
 - where: Table 1

LIMITS
- No limitations section. The ethics statement concedes that aggregating information per entity may pool private or sensitive content or expose documents to unpermitted users. It recommends building a separate map per permission level.
- Evaluated only on multi-document questions. The corpora are 2.8k-6.4k documents, with up to 20k in the scaling test. The three benchmarks are enterprise-style, partly synthetic or simulated (EnterpriseRAG-Bench, HERB workplace simulation, WixQA support articles).
- Several GPT-5.5/5.6 models and a hosted GPT judge are used, with a different judge only as a robustness check. The scaling and GLinker results are in a figure with no table. Cost is estimated.
- The Raw baseline's rank varies, with Luna at 53.85 and Sol at 67.69, so the gain depends on the model. On Sol the Raw baseline is already strong.
- The authors' own prompts and the map are built per corpus. Corpus2Skill and the other baselines are the authors' reimplementations.
- Oracle gold-document runs are noted as non-comparable.
- AI-use statement: generative AI helped with code and editing.

BUILDS ON: Graph RAG (Edge et al. 2024, arXiv:2404.16130) and HippoRAG (Gutierrez et al., NeurIPS 2024; 2025, ICML) are cited as the graph approaches whose structure stays inside the retriever and is not exposed to the generator. Also credited: LLM Wiki (Karpathy 2026, GitHub gist), Corpus2Skill (Sun et al. 2026a), EnterpriseRAG-Bench (Sun et al. 2026b), WixQA (Cohen et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.08643), HERB (Choubey et al., EMNLP 2025 Industry), GLinker (Stepanov et al. 2026), and agentic search work: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023), Self-RAG (Asai et al., ICLR 2024), Adaptive-RAG (Jeong et al., NAACL 2024), FLARE (Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023), and Li et al. 2026 (arXiv:2605.05242, direct corpus interaction).

CODE: Equation (1), p.4: G = (E ∪ D, L), L = {(e,d) | e ∈ E, d ∈ N(e)}. Algorithm 1, p.5, is the construction protocol, with steps INDUCETYPECATALOG, EXTRACTLOCALENTITIES, RESOLVE (LINK/ADD/UNRESOLVED), keeping entities linked to at least two documents, and RENDERENTITYPAGE. Candidate generation (p.18): BM25 over Entity Page text, pool their linked documents, rerank by BM25, and give the agent the top paths only (title, file path, document ID, with no content).

FIGURES
- Fig 2 (p.2): offline build and per-query traversal. It is the fastest way to see the Atlas example.
- Fig 1 (p.1): quality against cost per query.
- Fig 3 (p.8): incremental update savings.
- Fig 4 (p.9): corpus scaling, and the GLinker version without LLM calls.
- Fig 5 (p.17): amortised cost and break-even.
- Fig 6 (p.18): number of candidates.
- Table 10 (p.20) is a good worked case (Corpus2Skill fails to find two documents under one cluster; CorpusMap follows ENG-8192 → D1 → Serving Runtime → D2).
- Table 9 (p.19): the entity-entity edge case.

FIT TO NOTES
- generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/notes/11-retrieval-improvements.md has no entity-page or navigation-layer claim. Its only grep hit was "identity" in an unrelated sentence. Its sources frontmatter has no 2609.37226. It is an ablation on a production support agent with its own research items.
- notes/01-rag-pipeline.md section "Index-time structures: RAPTOR, GraphRAG, filesystems" (line 399, table at ~406) already covers GraphRAG and HippoRAG (line 412, via the Jiang survey). It says nothing about agent-facing entity pages. The finding that fits there is a navigation layer over files for an agent, not a retrieval index. The Table 3 comparison with HippoRAG/GraphRAG could sharpen that section, and the note already has the "filesystems" framing in its heading.
- notes/07-rag-in-production.md and 08-agentic-rag-prince.md mention entities only in passing. references.md has GraphRAG at 2404.16130 and the Kumar STAIR row (line 157), so a new row would sit near there.
- Verdict: no note already makes this claim, so it is new for 01-rag-pipeline (index-time structures) and could be cited in 11 only if the retrieval-improvements list gets an "entity-linked navigation layer" item. Worth noting is how much weaker that comparison is than the paper's agent-vs-agent results.

PROBLEMS: The extraction is clean. There are no embedded instructions. I have not checked arXiv id 2609.37226 against the PDF stamp beyond the header, which reads "arXiv:2609.37226v1 [cs.CL] 29 Sep 2026". Token costs and break-even points are read from figure labels, not tables. The extracted text file is at /tmp/jeong_out/t.txt (temporary).
